name: Abstract Expressionist ceramics
region: Los Angeles and Montana, United States
summary: American ceramics after 1954 in which the potter treats the vessel as a sculpture. Peter Voulkos threw large forms, cut, tore and stacked them, and painted them with the gesture of action painting.

philosophy.core_thesis: The pot is a place for a gesture: a thrown cylinder can be cut, torn and stacked like paint on a canvas, and the use of the vessel no longer sets the form.
design_principles: Throw large cylinders of 40 to 100 cm, in 3 to 5 parts, and join them while they are soft.
Cut, tear, paddle and puncture the thrown wall so that the action stays visible.
Stack the parts into a tall, uneven form, with open holes that show the inside.
Paint the clay with thick slip and iron in broad gestures, as an action painter paints a canvas.
Use thick, raw glazes: black iron, ash and tenmoku, with runs and bare clay patches.
Fire in a gas kiln in reduction at 1200 to 1300 °C; accept the cracks and the warps.
Leave a vessel opening, a lid or a spout as a sign of the pot, even when the pot cannot hold liquid.
Work fast and in a group, and call the studio a place of work, not a pottery.
anti_patterns: A smooth, perfect and useful table pot
A small pot with a pretty painted flower
Rustic craft that is made to look rough

form.shape: Large stacked pots, bottles with torn walls, big plates and chargers, lidded jars that are open, and sculptural vessels.
form.profile: A tall column of thrown rings with cut openings, a slashed surface, and a plate-like disc that is added at the top.
form.foot_and_rim: A heavy, wide base with a torn edge; the rim is cut or folded, not smooth.
form.proportion: Height 40 to 120 cm; the wall is 10 to 25 mm, thick enough to take cutting and paddling.
rules: Make the form at a scale of the body, not of the hand.
Keep the signs of cutting and tearing in the finished surface.
Leave one opening in the form, as a link to the pot.

bodies.rule: Use a coarse, grogged stoneware that can be thrown large, torn and stacked without slumping. A raku clay serves for small, fast pieces.

methods: cutting and tearing of the wall
stacking and joining of thrown parts
forming.joins: The parts are joined with thick slip and a wet hand, and the join is made part of the surface, not hidden.
forming.details: Torn edges, finger and tool marks, big cracks, glaze that pools and runs, and bare clay left in patches.

glaze.pattern: A broad gesture of black iron or thick white slip across a torn surface; a thick ash or tenmoku glaze that runs and breaks over the cuts.
glaze.gloss: Matt to gloss, 10 to 70 GU, with a large variation on one piece.
glaze.wear: The surface is robust; the bare clay patches darken with handling, and raku pieces are porous.

palette.strategy: Dark, earthy tones with a few high-contrast marks: black iron, white slip and rust, with raw clay.

firing.kiln: A large gas kiln that fires in reduction; a fast raku kiln for small pieces.
processes: throwing and stacking in one session
slow drying under plastic for 3 to 7 days
glaze firing in reduction at 1200 to 1300 °C
raku firing at about 900 °C for small works
firing.scale: One large piece takes a day to make and a week to dry; a firing holds about 10 big works.
firing.signs: Large cracks, warps, thick flows of glaze, torn edges and a heavy, uneven base.

pieces.form: Tall stack of five thrown cylinders with torn openings and bare patches
Large plate that is slashed and painted with black iron in one gesture
Vase with a torn wall, a thick ash glaze and a slip trail
Jar with a cut lid and a broken shoulder, covered in wax resist and glaze
Small raku bottle with a crackle black and a bare foot

positive: thick ash and tenmoku glaze runs
cracks and warps as part of the form

emotion.target_response: A feeling of energy and risk: the viewer sees a torn, heavy form and feels the force of one big gesture.

use_cases: a large sculptural vessel for a gallery
a museum label on 1950s American ceramic sculpture
avoid_when: the brief needs a useful table pot
the brief needs a refined, thin form

modifiers.how: Reduce the scale, keep one clear profile and use a single matt slip; drop the tears.
Close the form, add a use and a plain brush stroke, and smooth the surface.

wall_thickness.note: Large forms have a wall of 10 to 25 mm so that they can stand.
